25	## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
26	
27	The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. 29	Install the skill:
30	
31	```bash filename="Terminal"

33	```
34

38	Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
39	```
40	
41	## Or adopt by hand
42	
43	To adopt an existing app by hand:
44	
45	1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
46	2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
47	3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
48	4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
49	5. Optionally, [exclude cached content from a prefetch](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#exclude-content-from-a-prefetch) on the routes where caching content into the App Shell made it heavier than you want.
50	
51	Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
52	
53	## Enable Partial Prefetching
54	
55	> **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
56	
57	Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
58	
59	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
60	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
61	
62	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
63	  cacheComponents: true,
64	  partialPrefetching: true,
65	}
66	
67	export default nextConfig
68	```
69	
70	After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
71	
72	## What changes for `<Link>`
73	
74	| `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
75	| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
76	| `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
77	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
78	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
79	
80	The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
81	
82	## Migrate existing full prefetches
83	
84	Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
85	
86	A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
87	
88	> **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.
89	
90	### Verify prefetched UI with tests
91	
92	To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. Test the exact source link because different links to the same destination can use different prefetch settings:
93	
94	```ts filename="e2e/product-navigation.test.ts" highlight={7-16}
95	import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'
96	import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
97	
98	test('preserves the prefetched product summary', async ({ page }) => {
99	  await page.goto('/products')
100	
101	  await instant(page, async () => {
102	    const link = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
103	    await expect(link).toBeVisible()
104	    await link.click()
105	    await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/products/baseball-cap')
106	
107	    await expect(
108	      page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
109	    ).toBeVisible()
110	    await expect(page.getByTestId('product-summary')).toBeVisible()
111	  })
112	})
113	```
114	
115	Run this baseline against a production build with `partialPrefetching` disabled because automatic prefetching doesn't run in `next dev`. Then rerun the same test after adopting the destination. If it fails, the selected UI is no longer prefetched. Cache the reusable data or subtree that should stay available, then keep the passing test as regression coverage.
116	
117	### Static or cached content
118	
119	The output is already in the App Shell. Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`:
120	
121	```tsx filename="app/nav.tsx"
122	// Before
123	<Link href="/about" prefetch={true}>About</Link>
124	// After
125	<Link href="/about">About</Link>
126	```
127	
128	### Uncached content

138	```

268	### URL data
269	
270	[URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
271	
272	### Real-time content
273	
274	A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
275	
276	| Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
277	| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
278	| [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
279	| [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
280	| [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
281	| [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
282	| [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |
283	
284	## Adopting incrementally
285	
286	Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.

591	This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.
592	
593	## What "instant" means
594	
595	A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.
596	
597	> **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait.
598	
599	A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `<Suspense>` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition.
600	
601	Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `<Suspense>` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.
602	
603	<details>
604	<summary>Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI</summary>
605	
606	On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary in the full tree.
607	
608	On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger.
609	
610	This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load.
611	
612	</details>
613	
614	With `prefetch={true}`, per-link prefetching resolves a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) before navigation. First make the route instant with its App Shell. Per-link prefetching cannot fix a route that blocks without it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) for the patterns.

650	## The tools
651	
652	### Build the static shell
653	
654	With Cache Components, **caching directives** (`"use cache"` and its variants) assign a lifetime to an async function's result, which is what lets Next.js include it in the static shell.
655	
656	> **Good to know:** [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) is a variant for caching functions that read runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`. The result is cached in the browser only, not on the server. **It can't be part of the static shell.** See [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#use-cache-private) in the Optimizing prefetching guide for how it pairs with prefetching.
657	
658	**`<Suspense>`** declares fallback UI for parts of the tree that read uncached data or runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`; the content streams into the fallback when it resolves.
659	
660	> **Good to know:** A fallback may access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or the full URL. At build time, the fallback itself suspends, and a `<Suspense>` boundary further up the tree is needed. For a link with `prefetch={true}`, [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) makes URL data available before navigation, so the fallback can become part of the prefetched UI. Cached values like timestamps or data fetches can sit directly inside the fallback.
661	
662	Next.js can also generate an [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route, which renders during client navigations while remaining content streams. Partial Prefetching uses the App Shell as the default `<Link>` prefetch. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached content that depends on that link's URL data.
663	
664	### Prefetch URL data for a link
665	
666	Under [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), each visible `<Link>` prefetches the destination's App Shell by default. Links to the same route share one App Shell instead of triggering a separate App Shell request for each link.
667	
668	To prefetch the page content alongside the shell for a specific link, set [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch):
669	
670	```tsx
671	<Link href="/checkout" prefetch>
672	  Checkout
673	</Link>
674	```
675	
676	With Partial Prefetching enabled, `prefetch={true}` also opts the link into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching), which resolves the per-link URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, the full URL) ahead of the click.
677	
678	### Validate instant navigation
679	
680	By **default** (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. Validation surfaces what would keep navigations into a segment from being instant — which navigations would block, where a `<Suspense>` boundary is missing, and which data is reaching the user uncached.
681	
682	To opt out of automatic validation and only validate segments that explicitly export `instant`, set [`validationLevel`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#configuring-validation-defaults) to `'manual-warning'`:
683	
684	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={7}
685	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
686	
687	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
688	  cacheComponents: true,
689	  experimental: {
690	    instantInsights: {
691	      validationLevel: 'manual-warning',
692	    },
693	  },
694	}
695	
696	export default nextConfig
697	```
698	
699	<details>
700	<summary>How validation simulates different navigations</summary>
701	
702	For each validated route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy.
703	
704	For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks:
705	
706	- **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `<Suspense>` catches everything.
707	- **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation.
708	
709	Each case is validated independently. A `<Suspense>` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows.
710	
711	</details>

726	
727	To see the primitives in action, consider a small store app. Each product has its own page at `/store/[slug]`, reachable from the homepage and from other product pages. The goal is that navigating to and between products is instant.

729	The product page fetches two pieces of data: product details (name, price) and live inventory.

885	## Prevent regressions with e2e tests
886	
887	Validation catches structural problems during development, but as the codebase grows, the structural checks can only tell you that a shell exists. They can't tell you whether the right content is in it. E2E tests close that gap: they assert on what the user actually sees when the navigation completes, catching regressions before they ship.
888	
889	The [`@next/playwright`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@next/playwright) package includes an `instant()` helper for this. Install it alongside `@playwright/test`:
890	
891	```bash package="pnpm"
892	pnpm add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
893	```
894	
895	```bash package="npm"
896	npm install -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
897	```
898	
899	```bash package="yarn"
900	yarn add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
901	```
902	
903	```bash package="bun"
904	bun add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
905	```

907	A route can be reached two ways, and a `<Suspense>` boundary can cover one without covering the other:
908	
909	- **Initial page load**: Use `page.goto()` to test the static UI from the document response.
910	- **Client navigation**: Click a `<Link>` to test the destination's prefetched UI. [Per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) can add request-specific content to this UI.

966	## Fixing a navigation that blocks
967	
968	Consider a different route, `/products/[slug]`, that fetches product data from a public API and shows a featured list alongside:
969	
970	```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.tsx"
971	export default async function ProductPage(
972	  props: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>
973	) {
974	  const featured = await getFeatured()
975	  const { slug } = await props.params
976	  const res = await fetch(`https://next-recipe-api.vercel.dev/products/${slug}`)
977	  const product = await res.json()
978	
979	  return (
980	    <div>
981	      <FeaturedSection items={featured} />

983	      <p>${product.price}</p>

1090	### Iterate on loading states
1091	
1092	{/* TODO: diagram — before/after illustration showing a single high-up Suspense boundary being refined down to smaller boundaries closer to the data */}
1093	
1094	Validation passing means the navigation is instant. It does not mean the loading states are good. A `<Suspense>` boundary placed high in the tree (say, wrapping the whole page) might satisfy validation, but it replaces most of the page with a single fallback on every navigation.
1095	
1096	The best loading states keep as much real, cached content visible as possible and only show fallbacks where data is actually in flight. A product page that keeps the header, image, and description visible with only the price and availability behind a fallback feels faster than a full-page skeleton, even at the same total load time.
1097	
1098	Use the [DevTools](#visualize-loading-states-with-the-nextjs-devtools) to see what your users see, or see the [AI workflow](#ai-workflow) for automating the loop with an agent.
1099	
1100	## AI workflow
1101	
1102	At a high level, an agent optimizes a single navigation like this:
1103	
1104	- **Observe**: read validation insights and choose the exact navigation and UI that should appear immediately.
1105	- **Test**: confirm the target UI renders normally, then write an `instant()` test and verify that it fails before changing the route.
1106	- **Fix**: validation errors name a specific component and suggest a fix (`use cache` or `<Suspense>`). The agent applies the fix and re-runs validation.
1107	- **Verify**: run the test against a production-like build and keep the passing test as a regression guard.
1108	
1109	The agent doesn't need to understand the full caching model, only to follow the insights and errors until they're gone. It does need your app-specific intent, though. Tell it what should appear immediately, what can stream in, and what must stay fresh. When a caching decision is unclear, keep the data fresh behind `<Suspense>` rather than guessing a cache lifetime.
1110	
1111	For [iterating on loading states](#iterate-on-loading-states), a prompt like "maximize my content, and reduce the amount that needs to be behind a spinner" works well for pushing boundaries down.
1112	
1113	Agents working on a Cache Components route typically reach for three levers:
1114	
1115	- **Push down**: extract I/O into a Suspense-wrapped child so the parent stays static and static siblings lift into the shell.
1116	- **Cache**: pair `'use cache'` with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) to assign a freshness profile.
1117	- **Per-link prefetching** (nav-only): when a route reads URL data (`searchParams` or `params`), opt it into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) so the framework resolves that data at link-prefetch time. Session data from `cookies()` or `headers()` already lands in the App Shell without it.
1118	
1119	Each refactor should pair with a before/after capture to verify the change actually landed. Identical-looking captures mean the refactor didn't take effect.
1120	
1121	For agents to see what their changes actually render, pair this with [agent-browser](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser). With React DevTools enabled it reports the component tree and which `<Suspense>` boundaries are still pending, so an agent can make a change, snapshot the shell, check what landed, and adjust. See [Runtime visibility](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#runtime-visibility) in the AI agents guide for the setup.
1122	
1123	The [`next-cache-components-optimizer`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-cache-components-optimizer) Skill packages this loop. It confirms the target UI renders normally, writes an `instant()` test that fails before the fix, then works it to green against a production-like build and ships it as a regression guard. Use it for the initial load (hard navigation), client-side navigation (soft navigation), or both.
1124	
1125	## Opting out
1126	
1127	Not every layout or page can or should be instant. When the structural fix isn't worth the work, or when a route isn't a priority for instant navigation, refine validation at one of two scopes.
1128	
1129	The dev overlay surfaces this as the **Block** fix alongside every insight:
1130	
1131	<FixCardGrid>
1132	  <FixCard
1133	    group="block"
1134	    title="Allow blocking route"
1135	    href="/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-dynamic#allow-blocking-route"
1136	    snippets={[
1137	      { text: '// page.tsx or layout.tsx' },
1138	      { text: 'export const instant = false', highlight: true },
1139	    ]}
1140	  />
1141	</FixCardGrid>
1142	
1143	Set `instant = false` on the page or layout file. This opts the segment out of validation feedback. The segment may still navigate instantly if its structure supports it; the framework just won't surface insights for it. Navigations between sibling segments below are still validated.
1144	
1145	```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx"
1146	export const instant = false
1147	```
1148	
1149	With `false` on `/dashboard/layout.tsx`, validation no longer flags navigations into `/dashboard` from outside; navigations between `/dashboard/a` and `/dashboard/b` are still checked.
1150	
1151	For opted-out segments, the navigation blocks on the server. If the content depends on cookies or headers but has a known cache lifetime, caching it with [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) lets the App Shell carry it ahead of the click instead of opting out, as long as its [`stale`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#stale) time is at least 5 minutes.
1152

17	[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.
18	
19	To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.
20	
21	Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.
22	
23	> **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
24	
25	## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
26	
27	The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.

29	Install the skill:

33	```

41	## Or adopt by hand
42	
43	To adopt an existing app by hand:
44	
45	1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
46	2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
47	3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
48	4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
49	5. Optionally, [exclude cached content from a prefetch](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#exclude-content-from-a-prefetch) on the routes where caching content into the App Shell made it heavier than you want.
50	
51	Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
52	
53	## Enable Partial Prefetching
54	
55	> **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
56	
57	Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
58	
59	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
60	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
61	
62	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
63	  cacheComponents: true,
64	  partialPrefetching: true,
65	}
66	
67	export default nextConfig
68	```
69	
70	After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
71	
72	## What changes for `<Link>`
73	
74	| `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
75	| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
76	| `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
77	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
78	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
79	
80	The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
81	
82	## Migrate existing full prefetches
83	
84	Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
85	
86	A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
87	
88	> **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.
89	
90	### Verify prefetched UI with tests
91	
92	To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. Test the exact source link because different links to the same destination can use different prefetch settings:
93	
94	```ts filename="e2e/product-navigation.test.ts" highlight={7-16}
95	import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test'
96	import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
97	
98	test('preserves the prefetched product summary', async ({ page }) => {
99	  await page.goto('/products')
100	
101	  await instant(page, async () => {
102	    const link = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
103	    await expect(link).toBeVisible()
104	    await link.click()
105	    await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/products/baseball-cap')
106	
107	    await expect(
108	      page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Baseball Cap' })
109	    ).toBeVisible()
110	    await expect(page.getByTestId('product-summary')).toBeVisible()
111	  })
112	})
113	```
114	
115	Run this baseline against a production build with `partialPrefetching` disabled because automatic prefetching doesn't run in `next dev`. Then rerun the same test after adopting the destination. If it fails, the selected UI is no longer prefetched. Cache the reusable data or subtree that should stay available, then keep the passing test as regression coverage.

268	### URL data
269	
270	[URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. 272	### Real-time content
273	
274	A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.

279	| [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |

591	This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.
592	
593	## What "instant" means
594	
595	A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.
596	
597	> **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait.
598	
599	A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `<Suspense>` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition.
600	
601	Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `<Suspense>` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.
602	
603	<details>
604	<summary>Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI</summary>
605	
606	On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary in the full tree.
607	
608	On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger.
609	
610	This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load.
611	
612	</details>
613	
614	With `prefetch={true}`, per-link prefetching resolves a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) before navigation. First make the route instant with its App Shell. Per-link prefetching cannot fix a route that blocks without it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) for the patterns.
615

650	## The tools
651	
652	### Build the static shell
653	
654	With Cache Components, **caching directives** (`"use cache"` and its variants) assign a lifetime to an async function's result, which is what lets Next.js include it in the static shell.
655	
656	> **Good to know:** [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) is a variant for caching functions that read runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`. The result is cached in the browser only, not on the server. **It can't be part of the static shell.** See [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#use-cache-private) in the Optimizing prefetching guide for how it pairs with prefetching.
657	
658	**`<Suspense>`** declares fallback UI for parts of the tree that read uncached data or runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`; the content streams into the fallback when it resolves.
659	
660	> **Good to know:** A fallback may access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or the full URL. At build time, the fallback itself suspends, and a `<Suspense>` boundary further up the tree is needed. For a link with `prefetch={true}`, [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) makes URL data available before navigation, so the fallback can become part of the prefetched UI. Cached values like timestamps or data fetches can sit directly inside the fallback.
661	
662	Next.js can also generate an [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route, which renders during client navigations while remaining content streams. Partial Prefetching uses the App Shell as the default `<Link>` prefetch. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached content that depends on that link's URL data.
663	
664	### Prefetch URL data for a link
665	
666	Under [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), each visible `<Link>` prefetches the destination's App Shell by default. Links to the same route share one App Shell instead of triggering a separate App Shell request for each link.
667	
668	To prefetch the page content alongside the shell for a specific link, set [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch):
669	
670	```tsx
671	<Link href="/checkout" prefetch>
672	  Checkout
673	</Link>
674	```
675	
676	With Partial Prefetching enabled, `prefetch={true}` also opts the link into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching), which resolves the per-link URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, the full URL) ahead of the click.
677	
678	### Validate instant navigation
679	
680	By **default** (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. Validation surfaces what would keep navigations into a segment from being instant — which navigations would block, where a `<Suspense>` boundary is missing, and which data is reaching the user uncached.
681	
682	To opt out of automatic validation and only validate segments that explicitly export `instant`, set [`validationLevel`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#configuring-validation-defaults) to `'manual-warning'`:
683	
684	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={7}
685	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
686	
687	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
688	  cacheComponents: true,
689	  experimental: {
690	    instantInsights: {
691	      validationLevel: 'manual-warning',
692	    },
693	  },
694	}
695	
696	export default nextConfig
697	```
698	
699	<details>
700	<summary>How validation simulates different navigations</summary>
701	
702	For each validated route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy.
703	
704	For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks:
705	
706	- **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `<Suspense>` catches everything.
707	- **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation.
708	
709	Each case is validated independently. A `<Suspense>` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows.
710	
711	</details>

725	## A page that navigates instantly
726	
727	To see the primitives in action, consider a small store app. Each product has its own page at `/store/[slug]`, reachable from the homepage and from other product pages. The goal is that navigating to and between products is instant.
728	
729	The product page fetches two pieces of data: product details (name, price) and live inventory.
730	
731	- There is no `generateStaticParams`, meaning `slug` is only known at request time
732	- Both components await `params` to get the `slug`, which suspends. Each has its own `<Suspense>` boundary
733	- **Product info** rarely changes and is queried from the db using a cached function
734	- **Inventory** must be fresh on each request. The db query is inside a `<Suspense>` boundary

885	## Prevent regressions with e2e tests
886	
887	Validation catches structural problems during development, but as the codebase grows, the structural checks can only tell you that a shell exists. They can't tell you whether the right content is in it. E2E tests close that gap: they assert on what the user actually sees when the navigation completes, catching regressions before they ship.
888	
889	The [`@next/playwright`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@next/playwright) package includes an `instant()` helper for this. Install it alongside `@playwright/test`:
890	
891	```bash package="pnpm"
892	pnpm add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
893	```
894	
895	```bash package="npm"
896	npm install -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
897	```
898	
899	```bash package="yarn"
900	yarn add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
901	```
902	
903	```bash package="bun"
904	bun add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
905	```
906	
907	A route can be reached two ways, and a `<Suspense>` boundary can cover one without covering the other:
908	
909	- **Initial page load**: Use `page.goto()` to test the static UI from the document response.
910	- **Client navigation**: Click a `<Link>` to test the destination's prefetched UI. [Per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) can add request-specific content to this UI.
911	
912	```typescript filename="e2e/navigation.test.ts" highlight={6-14,20-25}

914	import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
915	
916	test.describe('Product page (/store/[slug])', () => {
917	  test('is instant on an initial page load', async ({ page, baseURL }) => {
918	    await instant(
919	      page,
920	      async () => {
921	        await page.goto('/store/hats')
922	        await expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('Baseball Cap')
923	        await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toHaveCount(0)
924	      },
925	      { baseURL }
926	    )
927	    await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toBeVisible()
928	  })
929	
930	  test('is instant on a client navigation', async ({ page }) => {
931	    await page.goto('/store/shoes')
932	    await instant(page, async () => {
933	      await page.click('a[href="/store/hats"]')
934	      await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/store/hats')
935	      await expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('Baseball Cap')
936	      await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toHaveCount(0)
937	    })
938	    await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toBeVisible()
939	  })
940	})

944	
945	Inside the callback, an initial page load shows the static UI and a client navigation shows the destination's prefetched UI. Other dynamic content remains blocked until the callback finishes.

948	
949	For client navigations, wait for the destination URL before asserting on its UI. Otherwise, a shared selector can match the source page before the destination commits. If the prefetched destination cannot commit, the URL wait times out and the test fails.

1100	## AI workflow
1101	
1102	At a high level, an agent optimizes a single navigation like this:
1103	
1104	- **Observe**: read validation insights and choose the exact navigation and UI that should appear immediately.
1105	- **Test**: confirm the target UI renders normally, then write an `instant()` test and verify that it fails before changing the route.
1106	- **Fix**: validation errors name a specific component and suggest a fix (`use cache` or `<Suspense>`). The agent applies the fix and re-runs validation.
1107	- **Verify**: run the test against a production-like build and keep the passing test as a regression guard.
1108	
1109	The agent doesn't need to understand the full caching model, only to follow the insights and errors until they're gone. It does need your app-specific intent, though. Tell it what should appear immediately, what can stream in, and what must stay fresh. When a caching decision is unclear, keep the data fresh behind `<Suspense>` rather than guessing a cache lifetime.
1110	
1111	For [iterating on loading states](#iterate-on-loading-states), a prompt like "maximize my content, and reduce the amount that needs to be behind a spinner" works well for pushing boundaries down.
1112	
1113	Agents working on a Cache Components route typically reach for three levers:
1114	
1115	- **Push down**: extract I/O into a Suspense-wrapped child so the parent stays static and static siblings lift into the shell.
1116	- **Cache**: pair `'use cache'` with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) to assign a freshness profile.
1117	- **Per-link prefetching** (nav-only): when a route reads URL data (`searchParams` or `params`), opt it into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) so the framework resolves that data at link-prefetch time. Session data from `cookies()` or `headers()` already lands in the App Shell without it.
1118	
1119	Each refactor should pair with a before/after capture to verify the change actually landed. Identical-looking captures mean the refactor didn't take effect.
1120	
1121	For agents to see what their changes actually render, pair this with [agent-browser](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser). With React DevTools enabled it reports the component tree and which `<Suspense>` boundaries are still pending, so an agent can make a change, snapshot the shell, check what landed, and adjust. See [Runtime visibility](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#runtime-visibility) in the AI agents guide for the setup.
1122	
1123	The [`next-cache-components-optimizer`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-cache-components-optimizer) Skill packages this loop. It confirms the target UI renders normally, writes an `instant()` test that fails before the fix, then works it to green against a production-like build and ships it as a regression guard. Use it for the initial load (hard navigation), client-side navigation (soft navigation), or both.

1127	Not every layout or page can or should be instant. When the structural fix isn't worth the work, or when a route isn't a priority for instant navigation, refine validation at one of two scopes.

When you click a project on the dashboard, its title now shows up instantly. The description and activity are no longer prefetched; they load after you click. `next build` passes, but I haven't tested this in a browser (prefetching doesn't run in `next dev`).

I followed the Next 16.4 docs bundled in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`:

1. **`next.config.ts`**: turned on `partialPrefetching: true`. Without it, `<Link prefetch>` would prefetch the whole page, including the details.
2. **`app/page.tsx`**: added `prefetch` to the dashboard's project links. By default, a link only prefetches the part of a page that's the same for every project, and the title differs per project. With `prefetch`, each link also fetches its own project's title ahead of the click. That works because `getProjectTitle` is already cached with `'use cache'`.
3. **`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`**: split the page into two sections, each with its own loading state:
   - **`ProjectTitle`** reads the project from the URL and renders the cached title, so the prefetch has it ready.
   - **`ProjectDetails`** starts with `await unstable_navigation()`. That keeps it out of every prefetch, so the slow `getProjectDetails` call (800ms) only runs when you actually navigate. Until then it shows "Loading details...". It stays cached for later visits.

Before, one loading state covered both the title and the details, so the title had to wait for the details.

Things to know:
- **Setting scope:** `partialPrefetching` applies to the whole app. That's safe here because no other links used `prefetch`. If you'd rather limit it to this one page, remove the setting and add `export const prefetch = 'partial'` to the project page.
- **Server cost:** each visible project link now makes its own prefetch request to the server. That's fine for a short dashboard list, but for a long grid you'd want to prefetch on hover instead.
- **First visit:** a direct page load, or a click before the prefetch has finished, briefly shows "Loading project..." instead of the title.
